business.what: Value hypermarket chain for middle- and lower-middle-income households, mostly in Tier 2 and smaller towns: apparel (44% of FY26 revenue), general merchandise (29%) and FMCG (27%). 74.1% of FY26 revenue came from 26 own brands (100% of apparel; ~73-74% of GM; ~60% of FMCG volume, ~35% of FMCG value). Stores average ~17,000 sq ft and are all leased (asset-light): rent is ~4.7% of revenue (Ind AS 116 adjustment Rs613 cr in FY26). Supply chain: one central DC and 17 third-party regional warehouses, moving to four regional hubs (a ~600k sq ft Haryana hub is running).
business.quickCommerce: Own app/website with hyperlocal delivery from 767 stores in 520 cities (Jun-2026), 14 mn registered users; 2-9% of a store's revenue (5% in most), ~5% of total revenue, cash break-even, ~70% grocery; 20% of its customers are new to Vishal (Q1FY27 call; Sep-2026 analyst meet).
business.formats: Large-format stores (LFS, 17-18k sq ft) plus a small format (~8k sq ft) piloted in UP and Haryana: 16 small stores at Jun-2026, same revenue per sq ft and ROCE as LFS (management). A new format for younger, slightly more affluent shoppers is in pilot (first store in Delhi).
business.src: AR FY26; FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations and calls; HSIE (25-Sep-2026)

q1fy27.sssgDrivers: New customers +7-8%, existing customers' spend +3%; fashion price points 13.9% SSSG; lower promotions lifted gross margin 30bp; minimum-wage increases in Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka lifted staff cost per sq ft ~13% (analyst, Q1 call).

guidance.stores: Analyst meet (Sep-2026): ~100 large-format stores a year with line of sight on ~400 over four years and room for ~1,200 more LFS (~2,000 in all); small formats incremental (runway ~4,000; 4-5 a quarter per Morgan Stanley). Q1 call: '80 to 100 store guidance' (analyst's words, not disputed). 833 stores at the Sep-2026 meet.
guidance.growth: Double-digit SSSG is the 'north star' (annual, not every quarter), volume-led; 18-20% revenue growth over the next 2-3 years (HSIE, 25-Sep-2026). Festive season falls in Q3FY27 vs Q2 last year.
guidance.margins: Gross-margin gains reinvested in product quality and price; ~50% of raw-material inflation absorbed by vendors; no price increases on opening price points; rent escalation ~15% every 3 years (~5% a year), so double-digit SSSG gives operating leverage (CFO, May-2026).
guidance.inflation: West Asia crisis: fabric prices +10-11% (May-2026); selective increases at higher price points only (Jul-2026).
guidance.src: Q4FY26 call (15-May-2026), Q1FY27 call (23-Jul-2026), analyst meet (Sep-2026, per HSIE 25-Sep-2026 and Business Today 24-Sep-2026)

history.event: Vishal Retail's debt-fuelled expansion (debt ~Rs700-730 cr by Jun-2010) ends in distress; TPG Capital and the Shriram Group buy its core business for ~Rs70 cr in Mar-2011. The old listed entity becomes V2 Retail (now a competitor); the acquired business becomes Vishal Mega Mart.
history.src: HSIE initiation (13-Apr-2026, from the RHP); AR FY26 legal-matters table (VRL / TPG Wholesale lease case)

history.event: Partners Group and Kedaara Capital buy VMM for ~Rs5,000 cr through Samayat Services LLP (controlled by Kedaara via Rishanth and Rishay Services LLPs); Rs4,284 cr of goodwill sits on the balance sheet. Gunender Kapur (ex-HUL) is MD & CEO.
history.src: HSIE initiation (13-Apr-2026, from the RHP); AR FY26 note 4

history.event: Airplaza Retail Holdings (multi-brand trading) and Vishal E-Commerce become wholly owned subsidiaries.
IPO: pure offer for sale of 102.6 cr shares at Rs78 (Rs8,000 cr) by Samayat; subscribed 27.3x; listed 18-Dec-2024 at Rs104 on NSE. No new money to the company.
Samayat sells ~19.4% in a block deal on 17-Jun-2025 (~Rs10,220 cr); holding 74.6% to ~54%.
Samayat sells 13.96% (65.25 cr shares) at ~Rs117 on 27-Feb-2026 (Rs7,636 cr); holding 54.1% to 40.1%. Buyers incl. Government of Singapore, HDFC MF, MAS.

Board reappoints Gunender Kapur as MD & CEO for 1-Sep-2026 to 31-Aug-2031; AGM (18-Sep-2026) votes on a 49.99% aggregate foreign-ownership cap so Airplaza's multi-brand business stays Indian-owned-and-controlled. COO Manoj Kumar left; Sashi Gumma replaced him (Jul-2026).
history.src: Business Today (24-Aug-2026); AR FY26 AGM notice; Q1FY27 call
